meta.definition: Biogenic CO2 point-source potential per country, Mt CO2/year: bioenergy CHP, power-only and heat-only plants >=5 MW, pulp & paper mills, and the biogenic share of waste-to-energy (biogenic share 61% assumed for P&P streams, 55% for WtE where unreported by the source). Data year 2023. Biogas-upgrading and bioethanol fermentation CO2 (high-purity but small per site, ~8-10 Mt/y EU-wide separated today) are NOT included - conservative for supply, optimistic for capture cost, since the included streams are mostly amine-capture flue gas; the capture-cost parameter is set on that basis.
meta.source: BECCS - Basics and Opportunities, BEST/Bioenergy Europe, April 2025, Tables 4-1/4-2 (EEA E-PRTR based); cross-checked against Rosa, Sanchez & Mazzotti 2021 (Energy Environ. Sci. 14:3086, top-5 country totals SWE 31 / DEU 28 / GBR 24 / FIN 23 / FRA 22 Mt/y for 2018 within scope differences).
meta.eligibility_note: All streams qualify as RFNBO carbon under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1185 Annex point 10(c) provided the underlying biomass meets RED II sustainability criteria and no double-crediting occurs (point 10 final subparagraph). Fossil industrial CO2 (point 10(a), eligible only before 2036/2041) is deliberately excluded from this file.
meta.caveats: SVK/SVN sector splits were ambiguous in the source table; SVK is set to 0.45 (range 0.2-0.7) and SVN to 1.3 (range 1.0-1.5), with their firm combined total 1.74 Mt/y. SAU/ARE/MAR have no mapped biogenic point-source inventory and are set to 0 (DAC-only), pending the export-case analysis.
